dimensions.assessment: Affects all entities responsible for the labeling or retail packaging of covered premoistened wipes sold in the United States, as well as consumers purchasing these products.
dimensions.evidence: The term ``covered entity'' means a manufacturer, wholesaler, supplier, individual or group of individuals, or retailer that is responsible for the labeling or retail packaging of a covered product that is sold or offered for retail sale in the United States.

dimensions.assessment: Requires redesign and clear labeling on product packaging to display specific 'Do Not Flush' warnings.
dimensions.evidence: A covered entity shall label a covered product clearly and conspicuously with the label notice and symbol

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue changes are specified in the text; enforcement is handled through existing FTC mechanisms.
Imposes new packaging and labeling mandates, assigns enforcement powers to the Federal Trade Commission, and explicitly preempts state and local labeling laws.
dimensions.evidence: No State or political subdivision of a State may directly or indirectly establish or continue in effect... requirements with respect to the ``Do Not Flush'' labeling

dimensions.assessment: Creates a permanent federal labeling requirement taking effect one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall apply to a covered entity beginning on the date that is 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific estimates of federal administrative costs for FTC enforcement are not provided.
Exact figures on the number of manufacturing businesses affected are not stated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes nationwide labeling and packaging requirements for premoistened, nonwoven disposable wipes and grants enforcement authority to the FTC, affecting wipe manufacturers and wastewater infrastructure.
